intent: Bound export-consent UI test scrolling with measured progress and real viewport visibility while preserving every original consent assertion and production behavior.

observedEvidence.uiResult: ChatExportDialogPrivacyTest records one skipped method after586.952 seconds; the second declared method has no verdict. Gradle Test Executor26 exits1 following OutOfMemoryError; the job itself did not time out.
observedEvidence.helperRisk: Repository-checksummed Compose ui-test1.12.1 performScrollTo repeats nonzero scroll corrections without an iteration or progress guard and discards the ScrollBy action return. Non-progressing layout can loop; this establishes a concrete test-helper risk, not the historical allocation cause.
observedEvidence.schedulerMismatch: The cached Compose1.12.1 v1 rule passes useStandardTestDispatcherForComposition=false, and its idle resource skips scheduler.runCurrent before the idle check. Supplying a custom StandardTestDispatcher can leave an accepted ScrollBy queued while idle sees no frame/recomposition work. The v1 empty-context factory uses UnconfinedTestDispatcher, matching the existing AppAuditContentTest fixture.

acceptance: Use an explicit360x640dp mdpi phone viewport and a finite maximum of eight actual ScrollBy actions.
Use the Compose v1 rule default composition dispatcher so actual scroll actions execute under its idle synchronization; change only this test fixture, without sleeps or clock-budget allowances.
Observe the real vertical scroll range and require positive progress after each action; require the target to be fully within the clipped scroll viewport and displayed before clicking.
Require actual scrolling in the primary consent flow so the fixture cannot make all scrolling assertions vacuous.
Retain the existing default redacted export, separate forensic preview/confirmation, no-early-export, and backing-out/no-resume assertions.
Keep production code, resource limits, test forks, timeouts, skip behavior and final publication gates unchanged.
Require both declared methods to execute successfully in completed current-source hosted Android XML; source review, API inspection or helper compilation cannot replace that execution.
limits: No heap dump or exact allocating stack was captured for the historical failure; its cause remains unproven.
The fixture tests local export-consent interactions, not physical device performance or every possible screen/font configuration.
